source: How Couples Meet and Stay Together (HCMST) 2009, Stanford University (Rosenfeld, Thomas & Falcon): public version 3.04 (waves 1-3) with wave 4, 5 and 6 supplements; U.S. adults with a spouse or partner, interviewed Feb-Apr 2009 and followed to 2017. External check: HCMST 2017-2022 (Rosenfeld, Thomas & Hausen), public version 2.2.
target: Probability that a couple together at the start of a follow-up period breaks up (divorce, separation or break-up of an unmarried couple) during that period; five periods from 2009 to 2017 (see periods). Partner deaths censored. A per-period probability, not an annual rate.
population: U.S. adults (English-literate, KnowledgePanel) with a spouse or main romantic partner in 2009: married and unmarried, different-sex and same-sex couples (same-sex oversampled); one partner's report of both
weights: Models are fitted unweighted, following the HCMST weights notes (Winship & Radbill) because of the GLB oversample; inputs include the main predictors of weight2. Descriptive rates are given with and without weight2.
how_to_combine: P(no break-up through period k) = product over j<=k of (1 - p_j), with p_j the model prediction for period=j, relationship_years and mean_age advanced by time_offsets[j], and all other inputs as of today. Period ends are about 1.1, 2.2, 4.1, 5.8 and 8.4 years after the start.

inputs.period: follow-up period '1'-'5' (see periods); the app sets it, not the user
inputs.relationship_quality: Excellent / Good / Fair / Poor or very poor: the reporting partner's answer to 'In general, how would you describe the quality of your relationship?'
inputs.couple_race: Both White / Both Black / Both Hispanic / Both Other / Interracial (Hispanic of any race; Other includes Asian, Native American and other)
inputs.party_pair: Both Republicans / Both Democrats / One Republican, one Democrat / Other or independent (either partner independent, other or no preference); leaners count as partisans for the reporting partner
inputs.how_met: Online / Through friends / Through family / Work or coworkers / School or college / Bar or restaurant / Church / Other (first match in that order; HCMST coding of how the couple met)
inputs.prior_marriage: Yes/No: the reporting partner was married before (the other partner's history is not recorded)
inputs.earnings: About equal / One earned more (income in the previous year)
inputs.religion_pair: Same religion / Different religions / One no religion / Both no religion (current religion, 13 HCMST categories)
inputs.parental_approval: Approve / Neutral or unsure / Disapprove / Not asked (no living parent): the reporting partner's parents' view of the partner
inputs.mean_age: mean of the two ages, years, AT THE START OF THE PERIOD: today's value + periods[k].start offset (time_offsets)
inputs.relationship_years: years since the romantic relationship began, AT THE START OF THE PERIOD: today's value + time_offsets[period]
inputs.edu_years_mean: mean years of schooling of the two partners (12 = high school, 16 = bachelor, 18 = master, 20 = doctorate/professional)
inputs.edu_gap: absolute difference in years of schooling
inputs.hh_income_k: household income, thousands of 2009 dollars (HCMST top code 175,000+ valued at 200)
inputs.children_in_hh: children under 18 living in the household

abstain: couples who are not currently together

boosting.label: Gradient boosting (comparison only, not exported)
boosting.reason: held-out log-loss gain over period-only 26.3% vs 25.5% for the additive core model, with overlapping intervals; not exported because the engine has no logistic boosting kind and the additive model is exactly explainable

rates_by_group.group: Married, quality: Poor or very poor
Unmarried, quality: Poor or very poor

population_reference.method: Survey-weighted (weight2) quantiles of held-out predicted probability of a break-up by each horizon, from 5x5-fold couple-held-out hazards averaged over repeats; all couples partnered at wave 1. Cells need >=100 unweighted couples (50-99 reported with small_cell=true); p5/p95 need >=200 and p1/p99 >=500, otherwise null. Aggregates only.

ood.method: squared Mahalanobis distance on the model inputs; percentile against held-out people (5 person folds)
